Hi Karthik / team,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is the security exhibit draft we pulled together for procurement (Brightwave-Security-Exhibit-Initial-Draft.docx) plus our SOC 2 summary. Two quick asks so we can keep the procurement window moving:

1) Can you confirm the acceptance criteria the exhibit requires (esp. around SOC 2 vs inspection rights)?
2) We need a proposed evidence cadence — Brightwave prefers quarterly sample deliveries and a rolling 12-month lookback. Can Redwood support that?

Also please highlight any redlines you anticipate so our legal team can evaluate timelines. We’re aiming to have the order form signed by end of month, so a 7–10 day turnaround on comments would help.

Date: 2026-07-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: acceptance criteria & evidence rotation

Team — looped in Brightwave so they see our proposed path. Initial thoughts:

- High level: Brightwave is asking for standard SOC 2 evidence plus some inspection/pen-test language. We should aim for a narrow, scoped inspection right rather than open-ended access.
- Evidence cadence: agree to quarterly delivery of agreed artifact packages (SOC packets, configuration snapshots, sampled logs) with a rolling 12-month archive—hosted as secure links.
- Pen test: allow customer-arranged pen tests only in a staging environment on a preset window, with vendor pre-approval and an agreed test plan. No ad-hoc production testing.

Action items:
- Laura: prepare a redline that limits audit rights to: SOC 2 report + scoped evidence deliveries + one scheduled inspection per 12-month period (or on agreed reasonable notice).
- Monica: propose a concrete evidence package (what files we deliver quarterly) and pen-test staging/access constraints.
- Vanessa/Marissa: call out commercial implications if they insist on broader inspection language.

I’ll draft a consolidated reply to Brightwave by end of day tomorrow.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-09T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: acceptance criteria & evidence rotation

Karthik / team — a few targeted redline points I’ll put into the draft (high level here):

1) Scope the inspection right: limit to evidence supporting SOC 2 scope and discrete security controls. No general "access to systems or raw customer data."
2) Notice & windowing: require >=72 hours notice for any interactive inspection; inspections to be limited to a pre-agreed 4-hour session unless otherwise negotiated.
3) Pen test language: allow a single customer-commissioned pen test in staging per 12 months, with vendor white-listing, a mutually agreed test plan, and a maximum blast radius (no DB writes, no exfiltration of production PII).
4) Data export: prohibit any capture of production secrets or key material; logs will be provided as redacted sets where required.

I will prepare redlines against their draft and include fallback language (e.g., additional evidence support at cost if they require more frequent inspections).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

(Attachment: redlines-karthik-2026-07-10.docx)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-10T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: acceptance criteria & evidence rotation

Technical notes to inform the evidence package / pen-test constraints:

- Quarterly evidence package (recommended minimal set): current SOC 2 report (PDF), system architecture diagram (redacted for internal-only IP), configuration snapshot (service-level, not secrets), sample audit logs for two representative days (redacted PII), and a summary of recent security events & remediation. Deliver via a pre-authenticated, expiring S3 link.
- Rolling retention: keep 12 months of delivered packages in our secure bucket for customer reference.
- Pen-test staging: we can provision a staging cluster with sanitized datasets. Vendor must be pre-approved and sign an NDA plus a test-plan. No direct access to production network or KMS.
- Evidence delivery cadence: we can commit to the quarterly package within 10 business days of quarter close. Faster delivery is chargeable as an SOC support add-on.

Practical constraints: we cannot provide live KV cache snapshots, unredacted request traces, or raw user payload dumps. If Brightwave insists, we should propose a limited-forensics engagement with specific scoping and cost recovery.

Happy to join a call with Brightwave to walk through the staging and evidence flow.

—Monica
Director, Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
(Attachment: pen-test-scope-proposal.xlsx)

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending the draft. Quick consolidated response and proposed next steps so procurement has what it needs: 

Summary of what Redwood can commit to today:
- Quarterly evidence package (SOC packet + redacted logs) with rolling 12-month access.
- One staged pen-test per 12 months with vendor pre-approval and signed test plan.
- Inspections limited in scope and windowed (>=72 hours notice; interactive sessions limited unless agreed).

Open items for your team to confirm:
1) Do you have a pen-test vendor in mind? If yes, please share contact and insurance/assurance info so we can start the pre-approval process.
2) Confirm if Brightwave will accept staged-testing only (no production testing).
3) Confirm whether the quarterly evidence cadence meets procurement’s approval or if they want monthly slices (this would be an extra support item).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- By 2026-07-12: Brightwave to confirm vendor + staging acceptance.
- By 2026-07-14: Redwood to deliver redline exhibit and detailed evidence checklist.
- By 2026-07-20: Target final order form ready for signature (DocuSign).

Would love to set a 30-minute sync — can we do Mon 7/12 at 10am PT?

Thanks,

Samantha / Brightwave — thanks for confirming vendor and staging constraints. Attached is Redwood’s redline of the security exhibit (redlines-karthik-2026-07-10.docx) which incorporates legal and security feedback:

Key points (summary):
- Audit rights narrowed to SOC 2 evidence + quarterly redacted evidence packages; one staged inspection per 12 months with >=72 hours notice.
- Pen-test allowed in staging only; vendor pre-approval required (SecureCheck Labs noted).
- No access to production secrets, KMS, or raw unredacted user payloads; we will provide redacted logs and architecture documentation as part of the package.
- Evidence delivery SLA: within 10 business days of quarter close; expedited delivery available as a billable service.

DocuSign link for the order form & exhibit: https://www.docusign.com/rw/BW-RF-2026 (link active for 14 days)

If that looks good, please countersign and we’ll kick off staging prep with Monica’s team. Thanks all for moving quickly on this.

—Karthik
